rules.name: SSH root login disabled
rules.explanation: SSH is configured to allow direct root login, which bypasses audit trails and increases brute-force risk.
rules.remediation: Set 'PermitRootLogin no' in /etc/ssh/sshd_config and restart sshd.

rules.name: SSH password authentication disabled
rules.explanation: SSH allows password-based login, which is vulnerable to brute-force attacks. Key-based authentication is more secure.
rules.remediation: Set 'PasswordAuthentication no' in /etc/ssh/sshd_config and restart sshd.

rules.name: SSH MaxAuthTries not set too high
rules.explanation: SSH MaxAuthTries is set higher than recommended, allowing more brute-force attempts per connection.
rules.remediation: Set 'MaxAuthTries 4' in /etc/ssh/sshd_config and restart sshd.

rules.name: SSH X11 forwarding disabled
rules.explanation: X11 forwarding is enabled, which exposes the X11 display to potential hijacking over SSH tunnels.
rules.remediation: Set 'X11Forwarding no' in /etc/ssh/sshd_config and restart sshd.

rules.name: SSH public key authentication enabled
rules.explanation: Public key authentication is disabled, forcing less secure authentication methods.
rules.remediation: Set 'PubkeyAuthentication yes' in /etc/ssh/sshd_config and restart sshd.

firewall.name: Firewall
firewall.command: echo 'UFW:'; ufw status 2>/dev/null || echo 'not installed'; echo '---'; echo 'FIREWALLD:'; firewall-cmd --state 2>/dev/null || echo 'not installed'; firewall-cmd --list-all 2>/dev/null | head -10; echo '---'; echo 'NFTABLES:'; nft list ruleset 2>/dev/null | head -15 || echo 'not installed'; echo '---'; echo 'IPTABLES:'; iptables -S 2>/dev/null | head -15 || echo 'not installed'

rules.name: Firewall is active
rules.explanation: No active firewall detected. The server has no host-level packet filtering.
rules.remediation: Enable and start the firewall (ufw enable, systemctl start firewalld, or configure iptables/nftables).

rules.name: No non-root UID 0 accounts
rules.explanation: Non-root accounts with UID 0 have full root privileges, bypassing access controls.
rules.remediation: Remove or change the UID of non-root accounts with UID 0.

sudoers.name: Sudoers
sudoers.command: grep -v '^#' /etc/sudoers 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^$' | grep -v '^Defaults' | head -15; echo '---'; ls /etc/sudoers.d/ 2>/dev/null

suid_binaries.name: SUID Binaries
suid_binaries.command: find / -maxdepth 4 -type f -perm -4000 2>/dev/null | wc -l; echo '---'; find / -maxdepth 3 -type f -perm -4000 2>/dev/null | head -10

rules.name: SUID binaries count under 50
rules.explanation: Unusually high number of SUID binaries. Each SUID binary is a potential privilege escalation vector.
rules.remediation: Review SUID binaries: find / -perm -4000. Remove SUID bit from unnecessary binaries.

security_updates.name: Security Updates
security_updates.command: if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf check-update --security 2>/dev/null; rc=$?; if [ $rc -eq 100 ]; then echo 'Security updates available'; exit 0; fi; elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum check-update --security 2>/dev/null; rc=$?; if [ $rc -eq 100 ]; then echo 'Security updates available'; exit 0; fi; elif command -v apt >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt list --upgradable 2>/dev/null | grep -i security && exit 0; elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper list-patches --category security 2>/dev/null | grep needed && exit 0; elif command -v apk >/dev/null 2>&1; then apk upgrade --simulate 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^(' | grep -v '^0$' && exit 0; fi; echo 'No security updates available'

rules.name: No pending security updates
rules.explanation: Security patches are available but not installed, leaving known vulnerabilities unpatched.
rules.remediation: Apply pending security updates: dnf update --security / apt upgrade.

reboot_required.name: Reboot Required
reboot_required.command: { [ -f /var/run/reboot-required ] && echo 'REBOOT_REQUIRED pending (/var/run/reboot-required)'; if command -v needs-restarting >/dev/null 2>&1; then needs-restarting -r 2>&1 | grep -iq 'needed\|required' && echo 'REBOOT_REQUIRED dnf needs-restarting'; fi; latest=$(rpm -q --last kernel 2>/dev/null | head -1 | awk '{print $1}' | sed 's/^kernel-//'); running=$(uname -r); if [ -n "$latest" ] && [ "$latest" != "$running" ]; then echo "REBOOT_REQUIRED kernel (running=$running latest=$latest)"; fi; } 2>/dev/null; echo 'DONE'

rules.name: No pending reboot for patched kernel or libraries
rules.finding: Pending reboot for patched kernel or libraries
rules.explanation: The host has applied updates that require a reboot to take effect. Kernel CVEs and library vulnerabilities remain exploitable until reboot.
rules.remediation: Schedule a maintenance window and reboot the host: sudo systemctl reboot. For zero-downtime on RHEL, consider kpatch/kernel live-patching.

auto_updates_enabled.name: Automatic Security Updates
auto_updates_enabled.command: { [ -f /etc/alpine-release ] && echo 'ALPINE_DETECTED'; if systemctl is-enabled unattended-upgrades 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^enabled'; then echo 'APT_AUTO=enabled'; fi; grep -hEs '^APT::Periodic::Unattended-Upgrade[[:space:]]+"1"' /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/20auto-upgrades /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/50unattended-upgrades 2>/dev/null | head -1 | grep -q . && echo 'APT_AUTO_CONF=yes'; if systemctl is-enabled dnf-automatic.timer 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^enabled'; then echo 'DNF_AUTO=enabled'; fi; if systemctl is-active dnf-automatic.timer 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^active'; then echo 'DNF_AUTO_ACTIVE=yes'; fi; if systemctl is-enabled yum-cron 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^enabled'; then echo 'YUM_CRON=enabled'; fi; } 2>/dev/null; echo 'DONE'

rules.name: Automatic security updates enabled
rules.explanation: Automatic security update installation is not enabled. Manual patching is delay-prone; auto-updates close known-exploit windows faster.
rules.remediation: Debian/Ubuntu: 'sudo apt install unattended-upgrades && sudo dpkg-reconfigure -plow unattended-upgrades'. RHEL/Rocky/Alma: 'sudo dnf install dnf-automatic && sudo systemctl enable --now dnf-automatic.timer'.

failed_logins.name: Failed Logins (24h)
failed_logins.command: if command -v journalctl >/dev/null 2>&1 && journalctl --no-pager -n1 >/dev/null 2>&1; then journalctl -u sshd -u ssh --since '24 hours ago' --no-pager 2>/dev/null | grep -ic 'failed\|invalid' || echo '0'; elif [ -f /var/log/auth.log ]; then awk -v d=$(date -d '24 hours ago' '+%b %e' 2>/dev/null || date '+%b %e') '$0 >= d' /var/log/auth.log 2>/dev/null | grep -ic 'failed\|invalid' || echo '0'; elif [ -f /var/log/secure ]; then awk -v d=$(date -d '24 hours ago' '+%b %e' 2>/dev/null || date '+%b %e') '$0 >= d' /var/log/secure 2>/dev/null | grep -ic 'failed\|invalid' || echo '0'; else echo '0'; fi

rules.name: Failed SSH logins under 100 in 24h
rules.explanation: Over 100 failed SSH login attempts in the last 24 hours, indicating a brute-force attack or misconfigured client.
rules.remediation: Investigate source IPs of failed logins. Consider firewall rules or VPN-only SSH access.

rules.name: SELinux or AppArmor is active
rules.finding: Neither SELinux nor AppArmor is active
rules.explanation: No mandatory access control (SELinux/AppArmor) is active. MAC limits damage from compromised services.
rules.remediation: Enable SELinux (setenforce 1 + SELINUX=enforcing in /etc/selinux/config) or AppArmor (systemctl enable apparmor).

kernel_security.name: Kernel Security
kernel_security.command: sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects net.ipv4.conf.all.send_redirects net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter kernel.randomize_va_space fs.suid_dumpable 2>/dev/null

rules.name: IP forwarding disabled
rules.explanation: IP forwarding is enabled, allowing the server to route packets between networks. This is a risk unless the server is intentionally a router.
rules.remediation: Set 'net.ipv4.ip_forward = 0' in /etc/sysctl.d/ and run sysctl --system.

rules.name: ICMP redirects rejected
rules.explanation: The server accepts ICMP redirect messages, which could be used to alter routing tables in a MITM attack.
rules.remediation: Set 'net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects = 0' in /etc/sysctl.d/ and run sysctl --system.

rules.name: ICMP send redirects disabled
rules.explanation: The server sends ICMP redirect messages, which could be exploited for traffic redirection.
rules.remediation: Set 'net.ipv4.conf.all.send_redirects = 0' in /etc/sysctl.d/ and run sysctl --system.

rules.name: Reverse path filtering enabled
rules.explanation: Reverse path filtering is disabled, allowing spoofed packets to be accepted.
rules.remediation: Set 'net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter = 1' in /etc/sysctl.d/ and run sysctl --system.

rules.name: Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) fully enabled
rules.finding: Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) not fully enabled
rules.explanation: ASLR is not fully enabled. Randomizing process address space layout makes memory-corruption exploits much harder to weaponize.
rules.remediation: Set 'kernel.randomize_va_space = 2' in /etc/sysctl.d/99-security.conf and run 'sysctl --system'.

rules.name: Core dumps from SUID binaries disabled
rules.finding: Core dumps from SUID binaries enabled
rules.explanation: SUID programs are allowed to produce core dumps, which can leak sensitive in-memory data to disk.
rules.remediation: Set 'fs.suid_dumpable = 0' in /etc/sysctl.d/99-security.conf and run 'sysctl --system'.

tls_ciphers.name: TLS/SSL Ciphers
tls_ciphers.command: ports=$(ss -tlnH | awk '{n=split($4,a,":"); print a[n]}' | sort -un | head -3); for port in $ports; do r=$(timeout 2 openssl s_client -connect 127.0.0.1:$port </dev/null 2>&1); cipher=$(echo "$r" | grep '^ *Cipher' | head -1 | awk '{print $NF}'); [ "$cipher" = '0000' -o "$cipher" = '(NONE)' -o -z "$cipher" ] && continue; proto=$(echo "$r" | grep '^ *Protocol' | awk '{print $NF}'); echo "Port $port: proto=$proto cipher=$cipher"; for wf in '-ssl3:SSLv3' '-tls1:TLSv1' '-tls1_1:TLSv1.1'; do flag=${wf%%:*}; name=${wf##*:}; wc=$(timeout 2 openssl s_client $flag -connect 127.0.0.1:$port </dev/null 2>&1 | grep '^ *Cipher' | head -1 | awk '{print $NF}'); [ -n "$wc" ] && [ "$wc" != '0000' ] && [ "$wc" != '(NONE)' ] && echo "  WEAK_PROTO: $name accepted (cipher=$wc)"; done; for wc in RC4 DES NULL EXPORT MD5; do nc=$(timeout 2 openssl s_client -cipher $wc -connect 127.0.0.1:$port </dev/null 2>&1 | grep '^ *Cipher' | head -1 | awk '{print $NF}'); [ -n "$nc" ] && [ "$nc" != '0000' ] && [ "$nc" != '(NONE)' ] && echo "  WEAK_CIPHER: $wc accepted ($nc)"; done; done; echo 'DONE'

rules.name: No weak TLS protocols (SSLv3, TLSv1, TLSv1.1)
rules.finding: Weak TLS protocols accepted (SSLv3, TLSv1, TLSv1.1)
rules.explanation: Weak TLS protocols (SSLv3, TLSv1, or TLSv1.1) are accepted on one or more ports. These are vulnerable to POODLE, BEAST, and other attacks.
rules.remediation: Disable SSLv3, TLSv1, and TLSv1.1 in all TLS-enabled services. Use TLSv1.2+ only.

rules.name: No weak TLS ciphers (RC4, DES, NULL, EXPORT, MD5)
rules.finding: Weak TLS ciphers accepted (RC4, DES, NULL, EXPORT, MD5)
rules.explanation: Weak ciphers are accepted on one or more TLS ports. RC4, DES, NULL, EXPORT, and MD5-based ciphers are cryptographically broken.
rules.remediation: Remove weak ciphers from TLS configuration. Use only strong cipher suites (AES-GCM, ChaCha20).

cert_expiry.name: Certificate Expiry
cert_expiry.command: ports=$(ss -tlnH | awk '{n=split($4,a,":"); print a[n]}' | sort -un | head -5); for port in $ports; do cert=$(timeout 2 openssl s_client -connect 127.0.0.1:$port </dev/null 2>&1); enddate=$(echo "$cert" | openssl x509 -noout -enddate 2>/dev/null | cut -d= -f2); [ -z "$enddate" ] && continue; if echo "$cert" | openssl x509 -noout -checkend 2592000 >/dev/null 2>&1; then status='ok'; else status='expiring'; fi; exp_epoch=$(date -d "$enddate" +%s 2>/dev/null); if [ -n "$exp_epoch" ]; then now_epoch=$(date +%s); days_left=$(( (exp_epoch - now_epoch) / 86400 )); else days_left=$status; fi; echo "Port $port: expires='$enddate' days_left=$days_left status=$status"; done

rules.name: TLS certificates not expiring within 30 days
rules.explanation: One or more TLS certificates will expire within 30 days. Expired certificates cause service outages and security warnings.
rules.remediation: Renew expiring TLS certificates. Consider automating with certbot/Let's Encrypt.

world_writable.name: World-Writable Files
world_writable.command: echo 'WORLD_WRITABLE_SCAN'; find /etc /usr /var -maxdepth 3 -type f -perm -0002 2>/dev/null | head -20 | sed 's@^@FILE:@'; find /etc /usr /var -maxdepth 3 -type d -perm -0002 ! -perm -1000 2>/dev/null | head -20 | sed 's@^@DIR:@'

rules.name: No world-writable files in sensitive paths
rules.explanation: World-writable files found in /etc, /usr, or /var. Any user can modify these files, risking configuration tampering.
rules.remediation: Remove world-writable permission: chmod o-w on flagged files in /etc, /usr, /var.

rules.name: No world-writable directories without sticky bit
rules.explanation: World-writable directories without sticky bit found. Any user can create, rename, or delete files in these directories.
rules.remediation: Set sticky bit (chmod +t) or remove world-writable permission on flagged directories.

cron_jobs.name: Cron Jobs
cron_jobs.command: echo 'SYSTEM:'; cat /etc/crontab 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^#' | grep -v '^$'; echo '---'; echo 'CRON.D:'; ls /etc/cron.d/ 2>/dev/null; echo '---'; echo 'USER CRONTABS:'; for user in $(awk -F: '{print $1}' /etc/passwd | head -100); do jobs=$(timeout 2 crontab -l -u "$user" 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^#' | grep -v '^$'); [ -n "$jobs" ] && echo "[$user]" && echo "$jobs"; done

ssh_keys.name: SSH Authorized Keys
ssh_keys.command: find /home /root -name authorized_keys -type f 2>/dev/null | while read f; do count=$(wc -l < "$f"); echo "$f: $count key(s)"; awk '{print "  " $1, $NF}' "$f" 2>/dev/null; done

docker_security.name: Docker Security
docker_security.command: if ! command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo 'NOT_INSTALLED'; else echo 'SOCKET:'; ls -laL /var/run/docker.sock 2>/dev/null; echo '---'; echo 'CONTAINERS:'; docker ps -q 2>/dev/null | head -8 | while read c; do docker inspect --format '{{.Name}}: privileged={{.HostConfig.Privileged}} user={{if .Config.User}}{{.Config.User}}{{else}}root{{end}} pid_mode={{.HostConfig.PidMode}} net_mode={{.HostConfig.NetworkMode}}' "$c" 2>/dev/null; done; echo '---'; echo 'INFO:'; docker info 2>/dev/null | grep -e 'Security Options' -e 'Runtimes'; fi

rules.name: No privileged Docker containers
rules.explanation: One or more containers are running in privileged mode, granting full host access and bypassing all security boundaries.
rules.remediation: Remove --privileged flag from container run commands. Use specific capabilities (--cap-add) instead.

rules.name: Docker containers not running as root
rules.explanation: Containers are running as root. A container escape with root privileges gives full host access.
rules.remediation: Set USER in Dockerfile or use --user flag to run containers as non-root.

rules.name: Docker socket not world-accessible
rules.explanation: The Docker/Podman socket has world-accessible permissions. Any user on the system can control containers.
rules.remediation: Restrict Docker socket permissions: chmod 660 /var/run/docker.sock. Ensure only docker group has access.

auditd.name: Audit Daemon
auditd.command: { systemctl is-active auditd 2>/dev/null; systemctl is-enabled auditd 2>/dev/null; } 2>/dev/null | head -2; echo 'DONE'

rules.name: Linux audit daemon (auditd) active
rules.explanation: The Linux audit daemon (auditd) is not running. Without auditd, security-relevant kernel events (privilege escalations, policy violations, sensitive file access) are not recorded, breaking compliance and incident response.
rules.remediation: Install and enable auditd: sudo dnf install audit (or apt install auditd) && sudo systemctl enable --now auditd. Consider deploying a ruleset such as Linux-Hardened-Auditd or neo23x0/auditd.

time_sync.name: Time Synchronization
time_sync.command: { v=$(timedatectl show --property=NTPSynchronized --value 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$v" ] && echo "NTPSync=$v"; for svc in chronyd systemd-timesyncd ntpd ntp; do s=$(systemctl is-active $svc 2>/dev/null); [ "$s" = active ] && echo "$svc=active"; done; } 2>/dev/null; echo 'DONE'

rules.name: System clock synchronized via NTP
rules.finding: System clock not synchronized via NTP
rules.explanation: The system clock is not synchronized with an external time source. Clock drift breaks audit log correlation across hosts, certificate validation, and Kerberos authentication. PCI-DSS 10.6.1 requires synchronized clocks.
rules.remediation: Enable a time service: sudo systemctl enable --now chronyd (RHEL) or systemd-timesyncd (Debian/Ubuntu). Verify: timedatectl show.

shadow_permissions.name: Shadow File Permissions
shadow_permissions.command: sm=$(stat -c '%a' /etc/shadow 2>/dev/null); gm=$(stat -c '%a' /etc/gshadow 2>/dev/null); pm=$(stat -c '%a' /etc/passwd 2>/dev/null); case "$sm" in ''|0|00|000|0000|400|0400|440|0440|600|0600|640|0640) echo "shadow_mode=OK($sm)" ;; *) echo "shadow_mode=BAD($sm)" ;; esac; case "$gm" in ''|0|00|000|0000|400|0400|440|0440|600|0600|640|0640) echo "gshadow_mode=OK($gm)" ;; *) echo "gshadow_mode=BAD($gm)" ;; esac; case "$pm" in 644|0644|444|0444) echo "passwd_mode=OK($pm)" ;; *) echo "passwd_mode=UNEXPECTED($pm)" ;; esac

rules.name: /etc/shadow and /etc/gshadow not world-readable
rules.explanation: /etc/shadow or /etc/gshadow is world- or group-readable. Offline password-hash cracking against these files is trivial for anyone with local access.
rules.remediation: Restrict permissions: sudo chmod 0 /etc/shadow /etc/gshadow  (preferred) or sudo chmod 640 /etc/shadow /etc/gshadow && sudo chown root:shadow /etc/shadow /etc/gshadow.

password_hashing.name: Password Hashing
password_hashing.command: { grep -E '^ENCRYPT_METHOD|^SHA_CRYPT_MIN_ROUNDS' /etc/login.defs 2>/dev/null; awk -F: 'length($2)>1 && $2 !~ /^[!*]/ { h=substr($2,1,3); if(h=="$6$") print "HASH=SHA512"; else if(h=="$y$") print "HASH=YESCRYPT"; else if(h=="$2" || h=="$2a" || h=="$2b" || h=="$2y") print "HASH=BCRYPT"; else if(h=="$5$") print "HASH=SHA256"; else if(h=="$1$") print "HASH=WEAK_MD5"; else print "HASH=WEAK_OR_UNKNOWN" }' /etc/shadow 2>/dev/null | sort -u; } 2>/dev/null | head -10; echo 'DONE'

rules.name: No weak password hashes (MD5 or crypt-DES) in /etc/shadow
rules.finding: Weak password hashes (MD5 or crypt-DES) in /etc/shadow
rules.explanation: One or more password hashes in /etc/shadow use a weak algorithm (MD5 or older). Modern GPUs crack these in minutes; accounts should be rehashed with SHA-512, yescrypt, or bcrypt.
rules.remediation: Set 'ENCRYPT_METHOD SHA512' (or 'yescrypt' on Debian 12+) in /etc/login.defs. Force affected users to reset their passwords so the new algorithm applies.

installed_packages.name: Installed Packages
installed_packages.command: OS_ID=$(awk -F= '/^ID=/{gsub(/"/,"",$2);print tolower($2)}' /etc/os-release 2>/dev/null); VID=$(awk -F= '/^VERSION_ID=/{gsub(/"/,"",$2);print $2}' /etc/os-release 2>/dev/null); MAJ=${VID%%.*}; D=Debian; R="Red Hat"; A=Alpine; case "$OS_ID" in debian|raspbian) [ -n "$MAJ" ] && D="Debian:$MAJ" ;; ubuntu) [ -n "$VID" ] && D="Ubuntu:$VID:LTS" ;; linuxmint|pop|elementary|zorin|kali|parrot) UBC=$(awk -F= '/^UBUNTU_CODENAME=/{gsub(/"/,"",$2);print $2}' /etc/os-release 2>/dev/null); case "$UBC" in bionic) D="Ubuntu:18.04:LTS" ;; focal) D="Ubuntu:20.04:LTS" ;; jammy) D="Ubuntu:22.04:LTS" ;; noble) D="Ubuntu:24.04:LTS" ;; esac ;; rhel|centos|fedora|ol|oracle|scientific|amzn|amazon) [ -n "$MAJ" ] && R="Red Hat:$MAJ" ;; rocky) [ -n "$MAJ" ] && R="Rocky Linux:$MAJ" ;; almalinux) [ -n "$MAJ" ] && R="AlmaLinux:$MAJ" ;; sles|suse) [ -n "$MAJ" ] && R="SUSE:$MAJ" ;; opensuse*) [ -n "$MAJ" ] && R="openSUSE:$MAJ" ;; mageia) [ -n "$MAJ" ] && R="Mageia:$MAJ" ;; alpine) [ -n "$VID" ] && A="Alpine:v$(echo $VID | awk -F. 'NF>=2{print $1"."$2; next} {print $1}')" ;; chainguard) A=Chainguard ;; wolfi) A=Wolfi ;; esac; { dpkg-query -W -f='${Package}\t${Version}\n' 2>/dev/null | awk -v e="$D" 'NF==2{print e"\t"$0}'; rpm -qa --qf '%{NAME}\t%{VERSION}-%{RELEASE}\n' 2>/dev/null | awk -v e="$R" 'NF==2{print e"\t"$0}'; apk info -v 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^\(.*\)-\([0-9][^-]*-r[0-9]*\)$/\1\t\2/p' | awk -v e="$A" 'NF==2{print e"\t"$0}'; pip3 list --format=freeze 2>/dev/null | awk -F== 'NF==2 && !/^#/{print "PyPI\t"$1"\t"$2}'; pip list --format=freeze 2>/dev/null | awk -F== 'NF==2 && !/^#/{print "PyPI\t"$1"\t"$2}'; } 2>/dev/null | sort -u

password_policy.name: Password Policy
password_policy.command: { if grep -qE '^passwd:.*\b(sss|ldap|winbind|nis|nisplus)\b' /etc/nsswitch.conf 2>/dev/null; then echo 'EXTERNAL_DIRECTORY'; fi; h=$(awk -F: 'length($2)>1 && $2 !~ /^[!*]/ {n++} END {print n+0}' /etc/shadow 2>/dev/null); [ "${h:-0}" = '0' ] && echo 'NO_LOCAL_PASSWORDS'; echo 'PWQUALITY:'; grep -hE '^[[:space:]]*(minlen|minclass|dcredit|ucredit|lcredit|ocredit)[[:space:]]*=' /etc/security/pwquality.conf /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/*.conf 2>/dev/null | head -10; echo 'LOGIN_DEFS:'; grep -hE '^[[:space:]]*PASS_MIN_LEN' /etc/login.defs 2>/dev/null; echo 'PAM_PWQUALITY:'; grep -hE '^[^#]*pam_pwquality\.so' /etc/pam.d/system-auth /etc/pam.d/password-auth /etc/pam.d/common-password 2>/dev/null | head -3; echo 'PAM_LOCKOUT:'; grep -hE '^[^#]*pam_(faillock|tally2)\.so' /etc/pam.d/system-auth /etc/pam.d/password-auth /etc/pam.d/common-auth 2>/dev/null | head -3; echo 'FAILLOCK_CONF:'; grep -hE '^[[:space:]]*(deny|unlock_time)' /etc/security/faillock.conf 2>/dev/null; } 2>/dev/null; echo 'DONE'

rules.name: Password minimum length
rules.explanation: Password policy does not enforce a minimum length of 14 characters. On hosts that don't use an external directory (LDAP/SSSD/AD/IPA) and have local password hashes, this means a local user could pick a short password that's trivial to brute-force.
rules.remediation: In /etc/security/pwquality.conf set 'minlen = 14' (or higher), or set 'PASS_MIN_LEN 14' in /etc/login.defs.

rules.name: Password complexity policy
rules.explanation: Password complexity policy is not enforced (no required character classes). On hosts that don't use an external directory (LDAP/SSSD/AD/IPA) and have local password hashes, simple passwords are easier to brute-force.
rules.remediation: In /etc/security/pwquality.conf set 'minclass = 3' or require characters via 'dcredit=-1 ucredit=-1 lcredit=-1 ocredit=-1'.

rules.name: Account lockout policy
rules.explanation: No PAM lockout module (pam_faillock or pam_tally2) is configured. On hosts that don't use an external directory (LDAP/SSSD/AD/IPA) and have local password hashes, failed login attempts aren't throttled — leaving the host vulnerable to sustained brute-force.
rules.remediation: Enable pam_faillock in /etc/pam.d/system-auth (or common-auth) and configure 'deny = 5 unlock_time = 900' in /etc/security/faillock.conf.

samba_config.name: Samba Server Config
samba_config.command: if command -v testparm >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f /etc/samba/smb.conf ]; then echo 'SAMBA_INSTALLED'; testparm -s 2>/dev/null | grep -iE '^[[:space:]]*(server signing|min protocol|server min protocol)' | head -5; else echo 'SAMBA_NOT_INSTALLED'; fi

rules.name: Samba server signing required
rules.explanation: Samba is configured without mandatory packet signing. Unsigned SMB traffic can be modified or replayed in man-in-the-middle attacks.
rules.remediation: In /etc/samba/smb.conf [global] set 'server signing = mandatory' and restart smbd.

rules.name: Samba SMBv1 disabled
rules.explanation: Samba is configured to allow SMBv1 — a deprecated protocol with known wormable vulnerabilities (EternalBlue, WannaCry, NotPetya).
rules.remediation: In /etc/samba/smb.conf [global] set 'min protocol = SMB2' (or SMB3) and 'server min protocol = SMB2', then restart smbd.

disk_encryption.name: Disk Encryption
disk_encryption.command: luks=$(lsblk -no NAME,FSTYPE 2>/dev/null | awk '$2=="crypto_LUKS"{print $1}' | head -5); [ -n "$luks" ] && echo 'LUKS_PRESENT' || echo 'NO_LUKS'; if command -v cryptsetup >/dev/null 2>&1; then for d in $(ls /dev/mapper/ 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^control$' | head -5); do cryptsetup status $d 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'type:.*LUKS' && echo 'CRYPT_MAPPER_LUKS' && break; done; fi

rules.name: Disk encryption (LUKS) active
rules.explanation: No LUKS-encrypted block device detected. Data on disk is not protected if the device is lost, stolen, or decommissioned without proper wiping.
rules.remediation: For new systems, enable LUKS during install. For existing systems, migrate data to a new LUKS-encrypted volume (cryptsetup luksFormat) — re-encryption in place is risky and not generally supported.

auditd_rules.name: Audit rules loaded
auditd_rules.command: if command -v auditctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then rules=$(auditctl -l 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$rules" ] || [ "$rules" = 'No rules' ]; then echo 'NO_RULES'; else echo "$rules" | head -30; fi; else echo 'AUDITCTL_UNAVAILABLE'; fi

rules.name: Audit rules loaded
rules.explanation: auditd is running but no audit rules are loaded — the daemon isn't recording any events. CIS recommends specific rules covering identity changes, sudoers, kernel modules, and privileged commands.
rules.remediation: Drop a CIS-style ruleset into /etc/audit/rules.d/ (e.g. 50-cis.rules) covering identity, time-change, sudoers, and execution events, then run 'augenrules --load' or 'systemctl restart auditd'.
